title: Your Phone Camera Can't See Color! 📸
description: Your camera sensor is color-blind! So how are your photos in color? Meet the millions of tiny cells and the clever filter inside your phone's camera.

scenes.say: Believe it or not, your phone's camera sensor can't see color at all. So how do your photos come out in color?
Light enters through the lens, which focuses it onto a tiny chip called the sensor, and the sensor measures how much light hits it.

scenes.label: In a 12-megapixel sensor
scenes.say: The sensor has millions of tiny cells. Twelve megapixels means twelve million cells, and each one only measures brightness.
scenes.image: File:CMOS image sensor chip-scale package oblique.jpg

scenes.title: The color trick
items: A colored filter on each cell
scenes.say: The trick is a colored filter over each cell: red, green or blue. Then your phone's processor blends neighboring cells to work out the real color of every point.

scenes.text: Half the filters are green, like our eyes
scenes.say: Did you know half of these filters are green? That's because the human eye is most sensitive to green.
